verdict.summary: Coda (now branded Superhuman Docs) has no OAuth for its REST API, which only takes personal API tokens, but its remote MCP server at coda.io/apis/mcp exposes a standard OAuth 2.1 server with dynamic client registration, PKCE and no app review, so any user can connect your agent the same day. The catch is that it's a beta MCP-only path with a single all-access scope (mcp:all) and tool names Coda says not to treat as stable.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: There is no console to register in: clients self-register at the registration_endpoint. Time is mostly wiring an MCP client with OAuth (many MCP SDKs handle discovery, DCR and PKCE).

timeToProd.assumes: Your agent reads and writes user docs through the Coda MCP server using OAuth; the REST API has no OAuth path, so the only alternative is asking each user to paste a personal API token.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: No review or listing step appears in any source we found. The metadata advertises open dynamic client registration.

prerequisites.item: An MCP client that supports OAuth discovery, dynamic client registration and PKCE (S256)
prerequisites.why: Coda's authorization server advertises a registration_endpoint, code_challenge_methods_supported S256 and only the authorization_code grant, so clients register themselves rather than through a console.

prerequisites.item: A Coda account for testing (any user who can open the docs you want to read)
prerequisites.why: MCP access is bounded by the connecting user's existing doc permissions.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Stated by staff in replies to the beta announcement.

prerequisites.item: An HTTPS redirect URI for your OAuth callback
prerequisites.why: Standard for the authorization code flow; you supply it during dynamic registration.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Coda's redirect URI rules (localhost, custom schemes) aren't documented in pages we could open.

scopeTiers.impact: Full read and write over everything the user can access in Coda via MCP tools. There is no read-only OAuth scope today.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: scopes_supported is ["mcp:all"] in both metadata documents, and the MCP endpoint's WWW-Authenticate header asks for scope="mcp:all". Staff confirm it's the single scope.

scopeTiers.tier: Personal API token restricted to MCP (no OAuth)
examples: API token with restriction: MCP (read, write, or read+write)
scopeTiers.impact: Users generate a token in account settings and paste it into your app. It's the only way to get read-only access, and it suits headless agents, but your users have to handle a secret.
The REST API takes bearer API tokens; the reference doesn't mention OAuth. Coda staff say the MCP has more capabilities than REST and there are no plans to bring them to REST.

steps.title: Fetch the OAuth metadata
steps.detail: GET https://coda.io/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/apis/mcp (resource and scopes), then https://coda.io/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server (authorize, token and registration endpoints).

steps.title: Register your client dynamically
steps.detail: POST your client metadata (name, redirect_uris) to https://coda.io/v4/api/oauth2/register. Store the client_id and secret it returns; the token endpoint expects client_secret_post.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Endpoint and auth method come from the metadata. We did not call the registration endpoint, so the response shape isn't confirmed.

steps.title: Implement the authorization code + PKCE flow
steps.detail: Send users to https://coda.io/v4/api/oauth2/authorize with response_type=code, client_id, redirect_uri, scope=mcp:all, state and an S256 code_challenge. Exchange the code at https://coda.io/v4/api/oauth2/token with the code_verifier.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Parameters follow the advertised metadata and the MCP authorization spec; Coda doesn't publish a dedicated OAuth guide.

steps.title: Connect and approve with a test account
steps.detail: Sign in to Coda in the browser when redirected and approve the 'Connect with Superhuman Docs' consent.

steps.title: Call the MCP server
steps.detail: Send MCP requests to https://coda.io/apis/mcp with Authorization: Bearer <access token>. List tools at runtime instead of hard-coding names.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: An unauthenticated POST returned 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="mcp" pointing at the protected-resource metadata.

steps.title: Store and use refresh tokens
steps.detail: Persist the refresh token per user so a server-side agent can keep working without the user present; staff describe approving once and storing the refresh token as the headless pattern.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Access and refresh token lifetimes aren't documented in sources we could open.

steps.title: Offer a PAT fallback for read-only or headless setups
steps.detail: Let users paste an API token created with the MCP restriction (and read-only if they want), since OAuth can't be narrowed below mcp:all.

steps.title: Go live
steps.detail: Ship the connect button. There is no listing, verification or review step for OAuth clients in any source we found.

agentCanDo: Read the OAuth and protected-resource metadata
Register the client via dynamic client registration
Implement PKCE, state checking, token storage and refresh
Discover MCP tools at runtime and handle schema changes
Write user-facing copy explaining the mcp:all access level
humanMustDo: Sign in to Coda and approve the consent screen for testing
Decide whether full read/write access is acceptable for your product
Create a dedicated Coda user and workspace if you want a service-style account
Generate an MCP-restricted API token where a PAT fallback is needed

blockers.symptom: 401 Unauthorized from https://coda.io/apis/mcp when using a personal API token
blockers.cause: The token wasn't created with the MCP restriction.
blockers.fix: Create a new API token and select the MCP restriction.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The specific 401 behaviour for unrestricted tokens comes from Coda's help article, which we couldn't open (403); staff confirm the MCP restriction is required.

blockers.symptom: You can't request read-only access in the OAuth flow
blockers.cause: The authorization server supports a single scope, mcp:all.
blockers.fix: Accept full access, or use a read-only MCP API token, or confine a dedicated user to a workspace with only the docs it should see.

blockers.symptom: Agent breaks after a tool is renamed or its parameters change
blockers.cause: The MCP server is in public beta and staff advise assuming tool names and shapes are not stable.
blockers.fix: Call tools/list at session start and map by description; add tests that alert on schema drift.

blockers.symptom: Feature you need exists in MCP but not REST (or the reverse)
blockers.cause: OAuth only covers MCP; REST v1 is token-only and lags MCP capabilities.
blockers.fix: Build on MCP for OAuth users; staff say there are no plans to port MCP capabilities to REST.

blockers.symptom: OAuth approval completes in the browser but the client stays stuck on authentication
blockers.cause: Client-side OAuth handling issues reported for some MCP clients (e.g. Cursor on Linux, ChatGPT without Developer Mode).
blockers.fix: Verify your redirect handling and refresh logic; fall back to a PAT if the client can't complete PKCE.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: User reports in the announcement thread, not confirmed by Coda.

nuances.text: Coda is being rebranded as Superhuman Docs: coda.io/developers now redirects to docs.superhuman.com, and the MCP resource is named 'Superhuman Docs MCP Server'. Expect more URL moves.
There is no bot or service-account concept; a token always acts as a real Coda user and inherits that user's doc permissions.
REST API rate limits are per user: 100 reads per 6 s, 10 writes per 6 s, 5 doc-content writes per 10 s, 4 doc listings per 6 s; exceeding them returns 429. MCP rate limits aren't documented.

Admins can't yet restrict individual MCP tools org-wide (e.g. delete tools) from Claude Team unless the server is in Claude's connector directory, which Superhuman said it was working on in June 2026.
The authorization server only advertises the authorization_code grant, with no client credentials grant, so a human approves each connection once.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: grant_types_supported: ["authorization_code"]. A refresh_token grant isn't listed although staff describe storing refresh tokens.

nuances.text: Coda's help-center articles on MCP setup and security returned 403 to our fetcher, so details such as OAuth admin controls and token lifetimes come only from community posts.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: help.coda.io and help.superhuman.com returned HTTP 403 on 2026-10-20.

Whether enterprise admins can block OAuth MCP connections (help center pages were inaccessible)
Redirect URI rules for dynamic registration (localhost, custom schemes)
